name: Bangalore to Mysore 1-Day Tour Package
overview: Mysore is the most-booked day trip out of Bangalore, and for good reason — in a single well-planned day you cover Srirangapatna's island fort, the Amba Vilas Palace with its gilded durbar hall, the Chamundi Hills viewpoint and the dancing musical fountain at Brindavan Gardens. Our driver handles the Mysore Road expressway run both ways so you spend your energy on the sights, not the driving.

The pace is full but comfortable: an early start, an unhurried two hours inside the palace, a proper lunch break at a restaurant of your choice, and the evening timed so you catch the fountain show before the drive home. It suits families with kids, first-time visitors to Karnataka and couples who want a packed day without an overnight bag.

faqs.question: Is the pickup time flexible?
faqs.answer: Yes. 6:30 AM works best because the palace and gardens both close in the evening, but we can start earlier or later — just tell us on WhatsApp and we'll re-plan the stops around your timing.

faqs.question: Are Mysore Palace entry tickets included in the price?
faqs.answer: No — entry tickets and guide fees at all monuments are payable directly by you. The palace ticket is inexpensive; our driver will drop you right at the gate.

faqs.question: Can we skip a stop or add one, like the Mysore Zoo?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. The car is yours for the day within the 300 km cap. Mysore Zoo, Karanji Lake or the Railway Museum can replace any stop — mention it to the driver in the morning.

faqs.question: What if we return after 10 PM or cross 300 km?
faqs.answer: Nothing changes for a normal day like this itinerary. If you add detours beyond 300 km, extra kilometres are billed at ₹12/km for a sedan — you'll always know before you commit.

name: Bangalore City Darshan 1-Day Package
overview: See the best of namma Bengaluru in one relaxed day — the Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, the hilltop calm of the ISKCON temple, Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace in the old pete, the 240-year-old Lalbagh Botanical Garden and the granite monolith of the Bull Temple. Between the big sights you drive past Vidhana Soudha, Cubbon Park and the UB City skyline, so you leave with a real feel for the city.

This package suits visiting parents, out-of-town guests, relocating families sizing up neighbourhoods, and NRIs on a short trip home. The routing is built around Bangalore traffic — north-side sights in the morning, the garden district after lunch — so you spend the day at the places, not between them.

faqs.question: Can we customise the list of places?
faqs.answer: Yes — this is a private cab, not a bus tour. Swap in Wonderla, Art of Living Ashram, Commercial Street shopping or a visit to relatives; we'll adjust the route as long as it fits the day and the 250 km cap.

faqs.question: Is this good for elderly parents?
faqs.answer: Very much so. Every sight has drop-off points close to the entrance, walking is optional at most stops, and the driver waits at each place so there's no rushing.

faqs.question: Do you provide a guide?
faqs.answer: The driver knows the city well and handles all the logistics, but he is not a licensed guide. Bangalore Palace has audio guides included with the ticket, and guides are available at Tipu's palace.

faqs.question: Can we start from the airport and end at a hotel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Airport pickup with a city darshan before hotel check-in is a popular option for transit visitors — the extra airport kilometres simply count within your 250 km allowance.

name: Nandi Hills Sunrise + Adiyogi 1-Day Package
overview: This is Bangalore's favourite pre-dawn escape done properly: watch the sun rise over a sea of clouds from Tipu's hilltop fort at Nandi Hills, explore the 1,000-year-old Bhoga Nandeeshwara temple at the base of the hill, and end the day at the 112-ft Adiyogi statue at the Isha Foundation centre near Chikkaballapur — staying on for the spectacular Adiyogi Divya Darshanam light show after sunset.

Because Nandi Hills demands a 4 AM start and Adiyogi is best after dark, doing both by cab is far easier than self-driving on no sleep. The package suits friends' groups, couples and photographers; the afternoon has a built-in lull for a long lunch or a vineyard stop, so it never feels like a forced march.

faqs.question: Is the 4 AM pickup really necessary?
faqs.answer: For sunrise, yes — Nandi Hills' entry gate queues up before dawn on weekends and the summit road closes to late arrivals once parking fills. If you'd rather skip sunrise, we can start at 7 AM and reorder the day.

faqs.question: Is the Adiyogi light show on every day?
faqs.answer: The Divya Darshanam show generally runs on weekend evenings and special days, and timings shift with season. Tell us your date and we'll confirm the schedule before you book.

faqs.question: Does the cab wait the whole day, even during the afternoon break?
faqs.answer: Yes. The vehicle and driver stay with you for the entire itinerary — the long lunch stop is your time to rest after the early start.

faqs.question: Can we add Skandagiri or a vineyard visit?
faqs.answer: A vineyard tour near Nandi slots in easily after breakfast. Skandagiri is a trek with its own pre-booking and timing, so it needs to replace the Nandi sunrise rather than add to it — ask us and we'll plan it out.

name: Bangalore to Tirupati Darshan 1-Day Package
overview: A same-day darshan of Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala is entirely doable from Bangalore with a disciplined plan — leave in the small hours, reach Tirupati by mid-morning, drive up the ghat road to Tirumala for your darshan slot, and be back home the same night. Our drivers do this run every week and know the ghat road, the queue complex drop points and the return timing cold.

This package is built for devotees who can't spare an overnight stay: working families, elderly parents accompanied by children, and groups fulfilling a vow. You book your darshan slot on the TTD portal; we plan the entire day's driving around it so the travel never becomes the worry.

faqs.question: Do you arrange Tirumala darshan tickets?
faqs.answer: No — darshan and seva tickets must be booked by you on the official TTD portal (tirupatibalaji.ap.gov.in). Once you have a slot, share it with us and we'll time the pickup and the entire day around it.

faqs.question: Which darshan slot works best for a one-day trip?
faqs.answer: A late-morning or early-afternoon slot is ideal with a 3 AM start. Very early slots need a previous-night departure — in that case consider our 2-day Tirupati package instead.

faqs.question: Is the Andhra Pradesh permit included?
faqs.answer: The permit is arranged by us but the fee (₹500–2,500 depending on the vehicle) is charged at actuals, as with tolls and parking.

faqs.question: Can senior citizens manage this trip?
faqs.answer: Yes — the cab takes you right up the ghat road to Tirumala, so there is no climbing involved. For a gentler pace with a night halt, the 2-day package is the more comfortable choice.

name: Tirupati 2-Day Package (1 Night Stay)
overview: The unhurried way to visit Tirumala: drive up on day one with a stop at the wish-fulfilling Kanipakam Vinayaka temple, rest overnight in Tirupati, and take your Venkateswara darshan fresh the next morning before an easy drive home. With a night's sleep between the journeys, early-morning darshan slots — the quietest of the day — become practical.

This itinerary suits elderly devotees, families with young children and anyone combining darshan with the other shrines of the Tirupati circuit — Padmavathi Ammavari at Tiruchanur, Srivari Padalu and the Silathoranam rock arch on the hill. The cab stays with you throughout, so temple-hopping needs no autos or waiting.

faqs.question: Is the hotel in Tirupati included?
faqs.answer: No — accommodation is excluded so you can choose anything from TTD guest houses to private hotels. If you'd like, we can suggest reliable options near the temple and you book directly.

faqs.question: How do we get darshan tickets?
faqs.answer: Book your darshan slot yourselves on the official TTD portal — slots open in advance and sell out fast. Share your confirmed slot with us and we'll build both days around it.

faqs.question: Should we stay in Tirupati or up in Tirumala?
faqs.answer: Either works. Tirumala stays (TTD accommodation) put you minutes from the temple for a pre-dawn darshan; Tirupati has more hotel choice. The cab drives you up whichever you pick.

faqs.question: Can we add Srikalahasti or the Chandragiri Fort?
faqs.answer: Srikalahasti (36 km away) fits on day 2 after darshan if you're comfortable reaching Bangalore closer to midnight; extra kilometres beyond 600 are billed at the standard per-km rate. Chandragiri Fort slots into day 1 evening easily.

name: Bangalore to Coorg 2-Day Package
overview: Two days in the Scotland of India: the gilded Namdroling Monastery at Bylakuppe, elephants at Dubare camp, the bamboo island of Nisargadhama, sunset from Raja's Seat, and a misty morning at Abbey Falls before the drive home. The route packs Kushalnagar's sights into the journey in, so you waste no daylight backtracking.

It's the classic first Coorg trip — right for couples, families and small friends' groups who want coffee-estate air without a long leave application. The pace leaves room for a lazy homestay evening in Madikeri, and everything on the itinerary can flex around your breakfast-to-sunset preferences.

faqs.question: Is the hotel or homestay included?
faqs.answer: No — stay is excluded so you can pick your own budget and style, from Madikeri hotels to estate homestays. We're happy to suggest options we've had good guest feedback on; you book directly.

faqs.question: Can we add Mandalpatti viewpoint?
faqs.answer: Yes, on day 2 morning — but the final stretch is a rough track where only local 4x4 jeeps are allowed. Our cab drops you at the jeep point; the jeep charge (around ₹1,500–2,000 per jeep) is payable there.

faqs.question: What does an extra day in Coorg cost?
faqs.answer: Roughly ₹4,500–5,000 more on a sedan (an extra day of driver bata, night halt and up to 300 km), and proportionately more for bigger vehicles. Tell us on WhatsApp and we'll quote the exact figure.

faqs.question: Is the drive okay for people prone to motion sickness?
faqs.answer: The highway run is smooth; only the last 30-odd km from Kushalnagar to Madikeri is winding. Sitting in front, taking the tablet before Kushalnagar and our driver's easy pace on the curves handle it well.

name: Coorg 3-Day Leisure Package
overview: Three days lets Coorg breathe. Beyond the Madikeri staples, you drive out to Talacauvery — the misty source of the Cauvery high on the Brahmagiri ridge — and Bhagamandala's triveni sangama, take the Dubare elephant camp at the right time of day, and still have slack for a plantation walk, a long Coorgi lunch or simply a second coffee on the homestay verandah.

This is the version for honeymooners, photographers and families who found the 2-day loop too brisk. Two nights in Madikeri mean you unpack once, and the return on day 3 collects the Kushalnagar sights at an easy pace instead of squeezing them into arrival day.

faqs.question: Are the two nights' hotel stays included?
faqs.answer: No, accommodation is excluded — Coorg's charm is in choosing your own estate homestay or resort. Both nights are in Madikeri in this plan, so one booking covers the trip; we can suggest options on request.

faqs.question: Is the Talacauvery road difficult?
faqs.answer: It's a proper but winding ghat road, about 90 minutes each way from Madikeri, and our regular sedans and SUVs do it comfortably. AC stays off on the steepest climbs, as on all ghats.

faqs.question: Can we swap a day for Mandalpatti or Chelavara Falls?
faqs.answer: Yes — day 2 flexes easily. Mandalpatti needs a local jeep for the last stretch (charged there), and Chelavara/Kabbe side trips work if you don't mind a longer day. Kilometres beyond 800 bill at the standard rate.

faqs.question: Can we do one night in Madikeri and one in Kushalnagar or an estate stay?
faqs.answer: Of course — the cab is with you throughout, so split the nights however you like. Tell us your stay plan and we'll resequence the sights to match.

name: Bangalore to Ooty 2-Day Package
overview: The Queen of Hill Stations in a weekend: drive through Bandipur's forest corridor (elephant and deer sightings from the car are common), spend the afternoon boating on Ooty Lake and wandering the Government Botanical Garden, then take on Doddabetta — the highest point in the Nilgiris — a tea factory tour and Pykara's lake and falls the next morning.

Two days is tight but genuinely workable for Ooty if the timings are respected, especially the Bandipur forest gate that closes to night traffic. Our drivers plan around it as a matter of routine. Best for couples and families with school-age kids who want maximum hill station per day of leave.

faqs.question: Why does the return start at 2:30 PM on day 2?
faqs.answer: The Bandipur–Mudumalai forest highway is closed to traffic from 9 PM to 6 AM. Leaving Ooty by mid-afternoon clears the forest comfortably before the gate; a later start would force the much longer Nice-road-free detour.

faqs.question: Can we ride the Nilgiri toy train?
faqs.answer: Yes — the popular Ooty–Coonoor stretch can be slotted into day 2 morning. Book seats in advance on IRCTC (they sell out early); the cab meets you at Coonoor station and continues the sightseeing from there.

faqs.question: Is the hotel included, and where should we stay?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is excluded — anything near Charring Cross or the lake keeps you central. We'll happily suggest options guests have liked; you book directly.

faqs.question: Will the ghat roads trouble kids or elderly travellers?
faqs.answer: The climb from Bandipur to Ooty is the classic 36-hairpin ghat. Our drivers take it slow and steady, and a front seat plus a motion-sickness tablet before the climb sorts out most travellers. AC is off on the steep sections for safety.

name: Ooty + Mysore 3-Day Package
overview: Two of South India's greatest hits in one loop: royal Mysore on day one — Srirangapatna, the Palace, Chamundi Hills — then over the Bandipur forest and up the 36-hairpin ghat to Ooty for a full hill-station day of Doddabetta, tea gardens, the lake and the Botanical Garden before the run home. Because Mysore sits exactly on the Ooty road, you see both without a wasted kilometre.

The 3-day pacing turns what would be two rushed trips into one comfortable circuit — a night in Mysore (catch the Palace illumination on Sundays and holidays) and a night in Ooty. Ideal for visiting relatives, first-timers to Karnataka–Tamil Nadu, and families mixing heritage with hills.

faqs.question: Can we reverse the loop and do Ooty first?
faqs.answer: Yes, though we recommend Mysore first: it front-loads the light sightseeing, puts the forest crossing in daylight both ways, and saves the cool hill mornings for Ooty.

faqs.question: Is Brindavan Gardens part of this package?
faqs.answer: It's not in the default plan since day 1 evening goes to the Palace illumination, but it can replace that slot — the gardens are 20 km from Mysore city and the fountain show runs after sunset.

faqs.question: How much driving is this per day?
faqs.answer: Day 1 is about 150 km, day 2 around 160 km with the ghat climb, and day 3 is the long one at roughly 290 km back to Bangalore. All within the 850 km package allowance for the standard itinerary.

name: Mysore + Coorg 3-Day Package
overview: Palace city and coffee country in a single sweep — day one covers Srirangapatna, Mysore Palace, Chamundi Hills and the Brindavan Gardens fountain show; day two climbs from the plains into Kodagu via Bylakuppe's Golden Temple and Dubare's elephants; day three gives Madikeri's falls, fort and Raja's Seat before an easy run home. Mysore sits right on the Coorg road, so the circuit is naturally efficient.

This is our most balanced 3-day itinerary — heritage, wildlife, waterfalls and hill air without any single monster driving day. It suits parents and kids, visiting in-laws, and anyone who wants variety over depth. Nights are split one each in Mysore and Madikeri.

faqs.question: Coorg first or Mysore first?
faqs.answer: Mysore first works better: the palace and gardens have fixed evening timings, while Coorg's sights are open all day, making day 3's return more flexible. We can reverse it on request.

faqs.question: What would an extra day in Coorg cost?

faqs.question: Do you have child seats?
faqs.answer: Yes — we can fit a child seat in any sedan or SUV on request at no extra charge. Mention the child's age when you book so we bring the right one.

name: Mysore + Ooty + Coorg 4-Day Grand Tour
overview: The grand South Karnataka–Nilgiris circuit: Mysore's palaces, Bandipur's forests, Ooty's peaks and tea gardens, and Coorg's coffee hills — one loop, one cab, four days. The geography works beautifully in this order, with Mysore as the gateway, the forest crossing into Ooty, and the Gonikoppal road bringing you across to Madikeri without retracing a single highway.

With three nights (Mysore, Ooty, Madikeri) and no repeated roads, this suits honeymooners on a week off, overseas visitors doing South India properly, and multi-generation family groups in an Innova or Tempo Traveller. Day lengths are deliberately uneven — heavier driving early, lighter final day — so the trip winds down rather than wears out.

faqs.question: Which vehicle do you recommend for this circuit?
faqs.answer: For 4 days and 1,100 km with ghats, an Innova/Innova Crysta is the sweet spot for families of 4–6 — the extra space matters on the long day 3. Groups of 8+ should take the Tempo Traveller.

faqs.question: Does the Ooty–Coorg road go through forest? Any timing limits?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Gudalur–Kutta stretch passes forest fringes and is best crossed in daylight, which is why day 3 starts early. Our itinerary keeps every forest section within safe daytime hours.

faqs.question: Can we extend to 5 days?
faqs.answer: Easily — an extra night in Coorg (Talacauvery day) or Ooty (Coonoor day) costs roughly ₹4,500–5,500 more on a sedan, proportionately more for larger vehicles. We'll re-quote the exact total on WhatsApp.

name: Bangalore to Chikmagalur 2-Day Package
overview: Coffee's birthplace in India makes a superb two-day trip: Hoysala masterpieces at Belur on the way in, an evening in Chikmagalur's cafe-and-estate country, then a big mountain morning — Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's highest peak, the sacred caves of Baba Budangiri and the spray of Jhari Falls — before the drive home. The scenery shifts from plains to shola grasslands within a single morning.

It suits trekkers who want summit views without a full trek (the road reaches near the top of Mullayanagiri), couples chasing estate stays, and anyone who found Coorg too crowded on long weekends. The itinerary trades a packed checklist for two or three big, memorable stops a day.

faqs.question: Can our cab drive all the way up Mullayanagiri and Baba Budangiri?
faqs.answer: The tarred road takes you to the parking below each summit — from there it's a short flight of steps at Mullayanagiri. The Baba Budangiri ridge road is narrow but fine for sedans and SUVs in normal weather; in heavy monsoon we adjust the plan.

faqs.question: Is Halebidu included?
faqs.answer: Belur is on the default route; Halebidu is 16 km further and adds about an hour — most guests add it on day 1 and push check-in slightly. It's within your 600 km allowance, so there's usually no extra charge.

faqs.question: What about Hebbe Falls or Kemmangundi?
faqs.answer: Both are gorgeous but need a full extra half-day and rough-road jeeps beyond Kemmangundi. If they're priorities, we suggest converting this into a 3-day trip — ask us for the revised quote.

faqs.question: Is the hotel included?
faqs.answer: No — Chikmagalur's estate homestays are half the experience, so we leave the choice and booking to you. We can share a shortlist that works well with this itinerary.

name: Bangalore to Wayanad 2-Day Package
overview: Kerala's green highland district in a weekend: cross the Bandipur–Muthanga wildlife corridor by morning, climb to the neolithic carvings of Edakkal Caves, drift around Karapuzha's backwaters, then spend day two among Pookode Lake's forests, the Lakkidi viewpoint hairpins and the vast curve of Banasura Sagar — India's largest earthen dam. It's a remarkable amount of Kerala for one night away.

Wayanad rewards early starts, and this plan is built around the forest checkpost timings on both sides. Best for couples and small families; monsoon travellers get the district at its most dramatic, while winter brings mist over the tea. The night halt is at Kalpetta, central to everything.

faqs.question: Why the 5:30 AM start?
faqs.answer: The NH-766 forest stretch through Bandipur and Muthanga is closed from 9 PM to 6 AM, and morning crossings offer the best wildlife sightings and coolest driving. The early start also gets you to Edakkal before the afternoon queue.

faqs.question: Is the Kerala inter-state permit included?
faqs.answer: We arrange the permit; the fee itself (₹500–3,000 depending on vehicle class) is billed at actuals like tolls and parking.

faqs.question: Is Edakkal Caves suitable for elderly travellers?
faqs.answer: It involves a steady 30–45 minute uphill walk plus steep ladders inside — genuinely strenuous. Less mobile guests often relax at a plantation cafe below while the rest climb; we can also swap the stop for Soochipara Falls.

faqs.question: Can we add Kuruva Island or Soochipara Falls?
faqs.answer: One of them fits if you're happy trimming elsewhere — Kuruva (seasonal, closed in high monsoon) suits day 1, Soochipara suits day 2 morning. Extra kilometres beyond 600 bill at the standard per-km rate.

name: Bangalore to Pondicherry 2-Day Package
overview: A weekend of French India: mustard-yellow colonial villas and bougainvillea lanes in White Town, the sea wall promenade at dusk, quiet minutes in the Aurobindo Ashram, the space-age Matrimandir at Auroville, and a boat across the backwaters to Paradise Beach. Pondicherry runs on a slower clock than Bangalore, and this itinerary is paced to match it.

The drive out via Tiruvannamalai's temple country takes about seven hours, so day one is structured as a gentle arrival into an unhurried evening by the sea. Perfect for couples, close friends and cafe-hoppers; families get a proper beach morning at Chunnambar on day two before the ride home.

faqs.question: Do we need to book anything at Auroville in advance?
faqs.answer: The Matrimandir viewing point pass is issued at the Auroville Visitor Centre on arrival; going inside the Matrimandir itself needs a concentration slot booked days ahead on Auroville's site — plan that yourselves if it matters to you.

faqs.question: Does the cab stay with us in Pondicherry?
faqs.answer: Yes, car and driver remain at your disposal both days — useful since Auroville, the boat house and White Town are spread across 15-odd km.

faqs.question: Is the Tamil Nadu permit extra?
faqs.answer: The permit fee (₹500–1,500 by vehicle class) is at actuals, on top of the package price, along with tolls and parking.

faqs.question: Can we return via Mahabalipuram?
faqs.answer: Yes — the East Coast Road detour through Mahabalipuram adds roughly 100–130 km and 3 hours. It's a brilliant add-on if you can accept a midnight drop; extra kilometres bill at the standard rate.

name: Bangalore to Kodaikanal 3-Day Package
overview: The Princess of Hill Stations deserves the full three days this package gives her: a scenic climb up the Palani hills on day one ending with sunset at Coaker's Walk, then a complete Kodai day — cycling or boating on the star-shaped lake, the eucalyptus hush of the Pine Forest, Pillar Rocks, Guna Caves and Green Valley View — before an easy descent past Silver Cascade Falls on day three.

At around 460 km each way this is the longest drive in our catalogue, which is exactly why the 3-day format works: the driving is confined to days one and three, leaving a whole untouched day at 2,100 m. Suited to honeymooners, groups escaping Bangalore summer, and chocolate-and-cheese pilgrims.

faqs.question: Isn't the drive too long? Why not fly or take a train?
faqs.answer: Kodai has no airport or railhead on the hill — every route ends with the same ghat climb. A private cab door-to-door beats the bus-plus-taxi shuffle, and our two-driving-day structure keeps it comfortable.

faqs.question: Are both hotel nights in the same place?
faqs.answer: Yes, two nights in Kodaikanal town — one booking, no repacking. Accommodation is excluded from the price; we can suggest options near the lake or Coaker's Walk on request.

faqs.question: What's the weather like — do we need warm clothes?
faqs.answer: Pack a proper jacket year-round: Kodai evenings drop below 10°C in winter and stay cool even in May. Monsoon (July–September) brings heavy mist — atmospheric, but plan indoor buffers.

faqs.question: Can we add Vattakanal or Mannavanur on day 2?
faqs.answer: Yes — Vattakanal's Dolphin's Nose walk or the Mannavanur sheep-farm meadows can replace the afternoon viewpoints. Mannavanur is 35 km out, still within the 1,000 km package allowance for most bookings.

name: Bangalore to Hampi 2-Day Package
overview: A weekend inside a UNESCO World Heritage Site: the boulder-strewn capital of the Vijayanagara empire, where the Virupaksha temple still holds worship after seven centuries, the Vittala temple's stone chariot anchors India's most photographed ruins, and sunset from Hemakuta Hill turns the whole valley gold. Day two covers the Royal Enclosure — Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables, the stepped tank — before the run home.

Hampi is spread over 25+ sq km, which is precisely where having your own cab and driver wins: you hop between clusters in minutes instead of haggling for autos in the heat. Suited to history lovers, photographers and families with school-age kids; carry hats and water — the site is gloriously shadeless.

faqs.question: Do we need a guide at Hampi?
faqs.answer: Strongly recommended — the ruins come alive with context. Licensed guides are available at Hampi Bazaar (roughly ₹800–1,500 for a half day, payable directly); our driver can help you engage one.

faqs.question: Where do we stay — Hampi or Hospet?
faqs.answer: Hospet (13 km away) has the widest range of proper hotels and is the default halt in this plan. Kamalapura and the island side have character stays too; the cab works with any of them.

faqs.question: When is the best season for this trip?
faqs.answer: October to February is ideal — daytime highs stay bearable and mornings are crisp. Summer visits still work with our early-morning-heavy itinerary, but expect 35°C+ afternoons.

faqs.question: Can we add the Anjaneya Hill (Hanuman temple) or Tungabhadra Dam?
faqs.answer: Anjanadri Hill across the river adds about 2 hours including the 575-step climb — doable on day 2 if you start at 7 AM sharp. The Tungabhadra Dam viewpoint is a quick stop already flagged in the plan.
